clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code note under 22 U.S.C. 254c (release point 119-121) prints Executive Order 12101 as amended by Executive Order 12608 as still provided, delegating to the Secretary of State the functions vested in the President by section 4 of the Diplomatic Relations Act (22 U.S.C. 254c); that statute remains in the Code, and no held instrument revokes the order.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Original text: the Secretary of State is designated and empowered to perform, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, the functions vested in the President by sections 4 and 6 of the Diplomatic Relations Act. Executive Order 12608 section 29 (September 9, 1987; 52 FR 34617) deleted the words naming sections 4 and 6 of the Diplomatic Relations Act (22 U.S.C. 254c and 254e) and inserted the words naming section 4 only, in the form "Section 4 of Diplomatic Relations Act (92 Stat. 809; 22 U.S.C. 254c)" as the U.S. Code note prints the amended order. Before the amendment the delegation covered sections 4 and 6; after it, section 4 only. The clause continues as amended, and the current U.S. Code note under 22 U.S.C. 254c still prints the order as amended.

research_rationale:
Identity: Executive Order 12101 of November 17, 1978 (43 FR 54195, FR Doc. 78-32799), held at the official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12101.txt. Its single paragraph designates and empowers the Secretary of State to perform, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, the functions vested or to be vested in the President by sections 4 and 6 of the Diplomatic Relations Act (92 Stat. 809; 22 U.S.C. 254c and 254e). Later instrument: Executive Order 12608 (September 9, 1987, 52 FR 34617), section 29, amends this order by deleting the words for sections 4 and 6 and inserting the words for Section 4 of the Diplomatic Relations Act (22 U.S.C. 254c). That strike-and-insert amendment is listed as a later event; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, so the delegation now covers section 4 only and the section 6 function (22 U.S.C. 254e) left the order on the date of the amendment. EO 12608 states no separate effective date for section 29, so the date used is its signing date, September 9, 1987. Ending search: the order has no duration, condition or sunset. The held corpus was searched for the number 12101: the only instrument that acts on this order is EO 12608 (the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification line, the Federal Register notice 2024-19192 and the U.S. Code note recite the order as amended by EO 12608 and do not revoke it). Current predicate: the held U.S. Code note under 22 U.S.C. 254c (release point 119-121, jobs/current-law/output/usc-notes) still prints the order as amended by EO 12608, and 22 U.S.C. 254c (section 4 of the Act) remains in the Code. Bounded searches read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121 text and notes, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML; no CFR hit for this order) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes; one hit, EO 12608).

savings.reason: No savings question arises. The order remains operative as amended, no ending, repeal or revocation is claimed, and the bounded searches found none; the one removed function (section 6 of the Act, 22 U.S.C. 254e) was removed by amendment, not by an ending that leaves residual effects.
